sentences.span: NDX ( -6.36%, worst day since March 9, 2020 (NDX -6.83%) in peak Covid drawdown.
sentences.why: GS confirms NDX -6.36%, worst since the Covid crash; a second Goldman piece (26077) gives the S&P ex-AI weekly figure.

sentences.span: At the bottom of the list sits the S&P ex-AI, down 0.3%.
sentences.why: Confirms the second clause of s1 (S&P 500 ex-AI down 0.3% on the week).

sentences.span: Weekend Prep (Brian Garrett): a positioning reset, not (yet) a systemic event... With US fundamental L/S net exposure at the 1st percentile (1y), he likes December upside call spreads
sentences.why: Goldman's own framing is that positioning had already been emptied (1st-percentile net exposure), which is why a strategist is willing to bet on a fast reset/bounce; corroborated by 25735's 'single digit hedge fund exposure to semis now.'

sentences.span: We expect a 0.16% increase in October core CPI (vs. +0.2% consensus).
sentences.why: Goldman's own CPI preview gives exactly 0.16% vs 0.2% consensus; Citi's two notes (25709, 25767) separately give 0.19%.

sentences.span: The catch is that the CTA number only holds if the market goes nowhere. Goldman's down-2.5-sigma scenario has $49 billion of S&P supply over a month, and a hot CPI is exactly the kind of catalyst that delivers one.
sentences.why: Matches the flat-tape (~$45bn/month) vs down-scenario ($49bn/month) CTA framing, with a hot CPI as the trigger; the same note separately has Sharkey saying a hot CPI 'likely confirms a hike,' supporting the December-hike clause.

sentences.span: S&P buyback demand is running at ~$5bn a day and 90% of corporates are in the open window Monday... the flat-tape CTA supply drops to roughly $2 billion a day, which the corporates comfortably outbid.
sentences.why: Matches the $5bn/day buyback figure, 90% window-open figure, and buybacks outbidding CTA supply in the flat/cool scenario.

sentences.span: Alec Phillips (Chief US Political Economist)... I think we could end up with a temporary moratorium that lasts several months until new rules can be put in place.
sentences.why: Matches the Goldman clause exactly; the UBS clause is separately confirmed.

sentences.span: Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has explicitly stated that all currently permitted data centers in Texas will be allowed to complete construction. Moreover, as she acknowledged in a New York Times interview this weekend she has limited ability to impose a data center moratorium.
sentences.why: Confirms the Hinojosa clause, correctly tagged (UBS) in the pulse.

sentences.span: The generic 30y spread widened 2.2bps on the day compared with an 8bp widening implied by the 4.4% move lower in SPX.
sentences.why: Matches figures (2.2bp vs 8bp implied, 4.4% equity drop) and bank (Goldman) exactly; GSIG30AS confirms IG.

sentences.span: $76bn issued last week, the 4th largest week of issuance in 2026 and the largest week in November ever
sentences.why: Two separate Goldman notes (25718 and 25719) both say the $76bn week was only the 4th-largest week of IG issuance in 2026 ('a record November opening' / 'the largest week in November ever') — not an unqualified record. The pulse drops that qualifier and states it as a flat record, overstating the superlative. The $67bn hyperscaler and $296bn YTD figures are accurate.

sentences.span: Credit has been under pressure for months as the AI spenders "reached deeper into credit funding to facilitate their capex plans", but Thursday's selloff hit the spending recipients.
sentences.why: Goldman's (Wilson's) explanation is that the equity selloff hit the recipients of data-center spending (e.g. chip/equipment suppliers), while the spenders (hyperscalers) are themselves the bond issuers whose credit stayed calm. The pulse inverts this into a split between 'companies spending on data centers' and 'the ones issuing bonds' as if they were different groups and as if the spenders were hit — but per the source the spenders are the issuers, and it was the recipients, not the spenders, whose stocks got hit.

sentences.span: Semis are now down ~28% over the last 1-month, one of the largest rolling, 1-mo drawdowns in history... AI/Semis in a rolling bear-market since this Summer - now ~40% off the highs
sentences.why: Matches 28% over 22 days (SOX), 'one of the largest...drawdowns in history', and ~40% off summer highs for AI/semis exactly.

sentences.span: NDX valuation bear market. Forward P/E now trades at 18.4x, well below the 5 & 10yr avg and its lowest level since 2020.
sentences.why: A fair compressed paraphrase of a genuinely reported valuation anomaly (lowest NDX multiple since 2020, and Goldman's research note pricing 'no growth' scenarios as still 'compelling' for AI-compute names); opinion-shaped but reflects banks' own framing, not an invented stance.

sentences.span: we believe stocks are now clearly in oversold territory... AI Compute: We favor NVDA and AVGO, which imply no growth from 2027... Semi Cap Equipment... we prefer AMAT & LRCX... Several global memory names (Samsung, SK Hynix...) with Samsung/SK Hynix now below total book.
sentences.why: Every element matches exactly: Goldman equity research (not a trading desk), oversold call, NVDA/AVGO with no growth past 2027, AMAT/LRCX preferred in equipment, SK Hynix/Samsung below (tangible/total) book.

sentences.span: August and September payrolls were revised higher, lifting the 3m average payroll growth to 137k, up from 51k prior to the data release.
sentences.why: Exact figures (137k from 51k) and bank (UBS) match.

sentences.span: This report keeps the Fed on track for a Dec hike.
sentences.why: Morgan Stanley clause confirmed verbatim; UBS's 25bp December-and-March hike call is separately confirmed in 26026 ('We expect another 25bps rate hike in December, and again in March').

sentences.span: neither weak enough to justify cuts nor strong enough to justify hikes... the Fed is already on track to hike in December due to inflation concerns.
sentences.why: Matches NISA's framing exactly: labor market justifies neither cuts nor hikes, December hike driven by inflation, not jobs.
